research_concepts: talent (regular-season net rating) as a confounder
methodological_questions: Does a team's adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predict series wins after controlling for roster talent?
Can a 54-series sample detect an adherence effect with useful power?
Can adherence be computed from pre-series information only, without outcome-derived labels or leakage from the series being predicted?
Is the data version (2025-26 playoffs incomplete as of 2026-06-16) handled correctly?

historical_evidence.finding: Tested BEST/AVOID run rates against series wins over 110 series-directions. Spearman BEST vs won rho=+0.131 (p=0.1723); AVOID vs won rho=-0.098 (p=0.3099). Recorded verdict 'null', failure type A_unanswerable, with INSUFF_EVIDENCE covering 91.5% of triggers. This is the closest prior test of the same question.

Tested pct_ran_BEST minus pct_ran_AVOID as a predictor of series wins with RS net-rating talent as a control. corr(talent, adapt)=+0.124. Per-series logistic: talent_diff_z +0.737 (p=0.0213); adapt_diff_z +0.328 (p=0.2755). Team-in-series cluster: talent p=0.0095, adapt p=0.2449. Univariate adapt beta=+0.311 (p=0.1128). Failure: after talent control adaptation p=0.275, and n~55 series cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality.

Playoff pivot-to-listed-counter sustainability across 12 pairs and 74 matchups. 10/12 pairs CONSISTENT and within 0.10 of non-pivot; no PIVOT_WINS. PNR->PULL_UP 1.069 vs non-pivot 1.224 (n_matchups=9) PIVOT_LOSES; DRIVE->PULL_UP 1.101 vs 1.217 (n=5) PIVOT_LOSES. Failure type B_powered_null.

Three-level counter ranking (population, team, matchup). The best counter is not stable across levels: L2 MIA disagrees with L1 on DRIVE. Playoff n_matchups 4 to 44. Failure mechanism unclear; auto_validation_status not recorded. Carries MECHANICAL_FLOOR and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER risks.

Team-level BEST vs AVOID PPP gap holds at the player-initiator level: mean gap +0.427 PPP over players with n>=10 per tier. Only 3 players clear n>=30 in both tiers. This concerns possession efficiency, not series wins.
Superstar suppression profiles. Rank-1 suppressor deltas are mostly within 1-2 SE, with no multiple-comparison control.
Only 2/30 stars (7%) have a stable top sequential suppressor across seasons (>=75% same top suppressor). Failure type B_powered_null.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Predicting series wins from team-level BEST/AVOID run rates (alignment with the recommended mix).
failed_approaches.why: Alignment-win Spearmans were not significant (p=0.172 and p=0.310) at n=110 series-directions. Recorded failure type A_unanswerable. Most triggers had insufficient evidence (91.5%).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Showing that adaptation quality (pct_ran_BEST minus pct_ran_AVOID) predicts series wins once talent is controlled.
failed_approaches.why: Adaptation p=0.275 per-series and p=0.245 clustered after talent control. Recorded failure type A_unanswerable: n~55 series cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality. Talent is the only term that reaches significance.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Pivoting to a listed counter after suppression as a route to higher PPP.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an adequately powered null: 10/12 pairs had population deltas under 0.10, and two pairs with signal were PIVOT_LOSES. Failure type B_powered_null.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Assuming a stable league-default best counter across population, team and matchup levels.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as inconclusive. Team-level disagreement with population level, small matchup cells, and failure mechanism unclear.

evidence_establishes: Two earlier studies of essentially this question, run on the same 55-series scope, returned null or untestable results: FAM:SF-APPS-030 (p=0.17 and p=0.31 for BEST and AVOID alignment) and FAM:SF-APPS-027 (adaptation p=0.28 per-series, p=0.25 clustered, after talent control).

Roster talent is the only predictor that reaches significance in the recorded series-level models (FAM:SF-APPS-027: talent p=0.021 per-series, p=0.0095 clustered), so talent must be a required control.

Play-type-level and player-level suppression signals in this project have mostly been small-n, unstable or uncorrected for multiplicity (FAM:SF-APPA-050, FAM:SF-APPM-022, FAM:SF-APPA-058, FAM:SF-APPA-048).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the adherence-to-win relationship would be detectable with a different adherence measure, a different series-level sample, or a pre-specified out-of-sample design.
Anything about 2025-26 playoff series, which were not complete on the question date (complete from 2026-06-21).
Causal effects of following the recommended mix. The earlier records are observational associations.
Whether the recommended mix itself was built without the outcomes it is evaluated on. The retrieved records do not state this.
own_inferences: The question as posed is nearly the same as FAM:SF-APPS-027 and FAM:SF-APPS-030, which were already run with the same 55-series scope and returned null or untestable results. Re-running it with the same design would most likely reproduce those nulls.

A 54-series test with a binary win outcome has very low power for effect sizes of the magnitude seen in the earlier records (adaptation beta +0.31, p=0.11 univariate). Any effect under a modest-to-large odds ratio is unlikely to be detected.

The adherence measure is probably built from the same play-by-play that defines the outcome (points and possessions), so an outcome-derived label and in-series leakage are likely unless the recommended mix is fitted strictly on data before each series.
Because the record notes 54 series as the sample, while the records cite 55, the unit count needs reconciling before any analysis.
uncertainties: Whether the recommended mix was fitted on data before each series (the retrieved records do not say whether a leave-one-series-out or time-ordered construction was used).
Series count discrepancy: data says 54 series; prior records say n=55 series / 110 directions.
Exact power under a pre-specified design; no power calculation was retrieved.
Whether the retrieved records' auto_validation_status fields (all NOT_RECORDED) reflect missing validation or unrecorded validation.
No record was retrieved on how the 2025-26 playoff data would be treated as of 2026-06-16, when it was partial.

historical_effect.explanation: Prior records show that this question, at this sample size and with a talent control, already returned null or untestable results (FAM:SF-APPS-030, FAM:SF-APPS-027). That moved the decision from a standard test to do_not_proceed as posed. Only a restructured, pre-specified, leakage-free test with talent control and an explicit power statement could be considered, and that test is unlikely to be powered with 54 series.

blocking_constraints.text: 54 series with a binary win outcome cannot reliably detect a modest adherence effect, and prior 55-series tests were null or untestable (FAM:SF-APPS-030, FAM:SF-APPS-027).
Roster talent confounds adherence and winning; FAM:SF-APPS-027 shows talent is the only significant term.
If the recommended mix or adherence is built with outcome-period data or the series' own possessions, the test is circular.
Suppression labels and BEST/AVOID classifications are derived from the same play-by-play used to define points and outcomes.

prior_work.summary: Earlier work by this project on the same 55-series scope tested BEST/AVOID alignment and adaptation against series wins (FAM:SF-APPS-030: null, untestable; FAM:SF-APPS-027: untestable after talent control). The question has therefore been partly answered as null or untestable at this sample size. A related playoff pivot test (FAM:SF-APPM-054) was a powered null. No record tests the question with a pre-specified, leakage-free design or on the 2025-26 playoffs.

risks.text: 54 series with a binary win outcome is far too few to detect a modest adherence effect; prior 55-series tests returned null or untestable results (FAM:SF-APPS-030, FAM:SF-APPS-027).
Team talent drives both adherence and winning. FAM:SF-APPS-027 shows talent is the significant term and adaptation is not once it is controlled.
The recommended mix must be fitted using only data before each series; any in-sample or future-period information inflates the apparent adherence effect.
Adherence labels derived from the same play-by-play as the outcome (points, possessions) create a circular association.

Many play types, counters and level-specific comparisons were tested across related families (FAM:SF-APPM-022, FAM:SF-APPA-050) with no multiplicity control; a researcher could select a favourable contrast.
Team-level BEST/AVOID rates depend on suppression triggers and minimum-count gates; a floor effect can produce apparent adherence differences (FAM:SF-APPM-055).
Most triggers have insufficient evidence (91.5% in FAM:SF-APPS-030), so adherence is measured on a small fraction of possessions.
Player-level and star-level gaps were not checked against placebo or matched controls (FAM:SF-APPA-048, FAM:SF-CHT-009).
Suppression and play-type effects differ across seasons (FAM:SF-APPA-058: only 2/30 stars stable), so pooling 2022-23 to 2025-26 may mix regimes.
Series win labels and team-in-series assignments must be verified; the record count (54 vs 55 series) differs.

design.estimand: Association between a pre-registered, pre-series adherence score to the suppression-conditional recommended mix and the probability of winning the series, conditional on pre-series regular-season net-rating talent. This is an association, not a causal effect.
design.unit: Team-series (one row per team per series), with series-level clustering by team.
design.sample: Completed playoff series from 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25, plus 2025-26 playoff series only after completion (on or after 2026-06-21). Exclude partial 2025-26 playoff series from any analysis dated 2026-06-16. The 54 vs 55 series count must be reconciled before analysis.
design.power: Not established. A power calculation for the pre-specified odds ratio must be run before analysis. With 54 series, the study is expected to be underpowered for the modest effects seen in FAM:SF-APPS-027 and FAM:SF-APPS-030; if the calculation shows less than 80% power for a clinically meaningful odds ratio, the study should be reported as exploratory.
design.controls: Pre-series regular-season net rating (talent), with a pre-registered team-level random or clustered term; opponent talent; home-court; series round. Recommended mix must be fitted only on pre-series data (leave-one-series-out or time-ordered), with no outcome-period possessions in the adherence score.
design.falsification: Placebo adherence from a random or shuffled recommended mix, and an adherence measure built from regular-season data only, to test whether any signal is specific to the mix and not roster or pace. Also test adherence on a non-outcome outcome (e.g., PPP in the mix) to check for outcome-derived leakage.
design.multiplicity: One primary contrast (adherence coefficient after talent control) pre-registered. All other play types, levels and secondary contrasts reported as exploratory with Holm or FDR correction.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the pre-registered adherence coefficient is significant at alpha 0.05 with cluster-robust SE after talent control, survives the placebo and leakage checks, and the power calculation supports the estimate. Otherwise report as null (if powered) or uncertain (if not). Do not report as supported on the basis of univariate association.
design.data_version: Data as of 2026-06-16: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13); 2025-26 playoffs excluded because they were partial until 2026-06-21. Re-run after 2026-06-21 only with a new version stamp.

methodological_questions: Does adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended offensive mix predict winning in playoff series?
What sample size and unit of analysis (54 series) are needed to test mix adherence against win outcome?
How should adherence be measured and separated from outcome-derived labels and team quality?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-06-16, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
Adhering to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
